answer: Sybil resistance rests on a staked-identity gate: each new key must post its own bond in quartz-denominated escrow before it can attest, and rewards flow to the bond, not the operator, so a clone earns nothing until that stake clears the floor. Voting weight comes from bonded history, not key count, so N puppets need N times the capital, and a cluster caught colluding forfeits part of every bond in it. Cost scales linearly with identities while yield stays flat, making an ember of real history pricier to fake than fresh keys. Each identity also burns gas and time, a barrier as solid as shale.
